final_candidates.decision_summary: A charge insertion at a conserved hydrophobic position is strongly incompatible with both the experimental backbone and sequence context, making major folding disruption likely.
Replacing V38 with an acidic residue is strongly disfavored by structural, sequence, and evolutionary evidence and should destabilize the local hydrophobic environment.
Proline at L65 is highly incompatible with the modeled backbone and sequence context and may disrupt the C-terminal structural element, although its terminal proximity adds uncertainty.

stop_reason.detail: Independent evidence dimensions converge on the selected mutations, and the remaining tools are unlikely to resolve the residual uncertainty enough to alter their ranking.

history.rationale: Replacing a bulky aromatic residue with proline is likely to disrupt local backbone geometry and hydrophobic packing.

The substitution is essentially implausible by the sequence model and absent from all homologs, but its structural incompatibility is only moderate relative to leading candidates. It remains plausible but is no longer Top-3.
Introducing a charged acidic residue at a hydrophobic aromatic position may strongly destabilize the folded core.
F40D remains structurally and sequence-wise unfavorable, but aspartate occurs in about 19% of covered homologs. That natural tolerance lowers confidence that it will reliably abolish folding.
Proline at this internal hydrophobic position may disrupt regular secondary structure and core packing.

I33P is strongly compatible with the experimental backbone and occurs in a substantial fraction of homologs. These signals argue that proline at this position may be tolerated rather than folding-disruptive.
A hydrophobic-to-charged substitution in the central sequence region is likely to create unfavorable packing or desolvation.

Introducing an acidic residue at V38 is strongly incompatible with the experimental backbone and sequence context. Its absence among covered homologs at a relatively conserved position further supports a disruptive effect.
Replacing phenylalanine with glutamate may disrupt an aromatic packing interaction and introduce a buried charge.
The sequence model disfavors F48E, but the structural model considers it comparatively compatible. MSA coverage at this site is limited, so evolutionary absence was not given substantial weight.
This aromatic-to-acidic change is physicochemically severe and could destabilize the protein interior.

Although sequence and evolutionary evidence disfavor Y34D, ProteinMPNN finds it compatible with the fixed backbone. This conflict suggests possible functional perturbation without reliable folding knockout.
Proline substitution within the adjacent aromatic-rich segment may perturb both backbone structure and aromatic packing.

Y18P is strongly disfavored by both structure- and sequence-conditioned models and is absent across all aligned homologs. Proline substitution next to the aromatic pair is therefore a strong folding-disruption hypothesis.
A proline near the C-terminal structured region may interrupt secondary structure and weaken overall folding.

L65P has very poor structural and sequence compatibility, consistent with proline disrupting the C-terminal structural element. Its absence from homologs with good coverage supports low natural tolerance.
Introducing a positively charged lysine at a hydrophobic position may impair core packing.

Despite low sequence plausibility and evolutionary absence, ProteinMPNN strongly favors lysine on the experimental backbone. That direct structural-context evidence makes a folding knockout unlikely relative to alternatives.

rejection.reason: Despite low sequence plausibility and evolutionary absence, ProteinMPNN strongly favors lysine on the experimental backbone. That direct structural-context evidence makes a folding knockout unlikely relative to alternatives.

history.rationale: The hydrophobic-to-basic substitution could destabilize a buried or tightly packed local environment.

The extremely poor fixed-backbone compatibility and sequence plausibility strongly favor structural disruption. Complete MSA coverage with no observed arginine adds evidence that this conserved hydrophobic position disfavors the substitution.
